stops.note: 'water of life', the alchemists' name for distilled alcohol; the medical school of Salerno produced some of the earliest clear European descriptions of distilling wine
a word-for-word Gaelic translation of aqua vitae (Irish uisce beatha); the Scottish Exchequer Rolls of 1494 record malt sent to Friar John Cor 'wherewith to make aqua vitae'
borrowed as usquebaugh in the 1580s and cut down to whisky by 1715; Scotch is spelled whisky, while Irish and most American makers write whiskey

current_meaning: a spirit distilled from fermented grain mash, especially from Scotland
